h1: Fence Repair in Dallas, TX: Posts, Pickets, Panels and Gates
heroSub: Leaning sections, rotted posts, missing pickets and storm damage, sorted by what each repair involves and what Dallas-area firms advertise for it. Get two or three written quotes from independent contractors before you commit.
introHtml:
Fence repair in Dallas, TX covers more than swapping a picket. A contractor's scope runs from resetting one post or replacing a board, through straightening a leaning section, up to rebuilding panels after a storm or rehanging a sagging wood gate. This page walks through each failure mode, what a repair scope normally lists, and when a contractor starts talking about replacement instead.

White Rock Fence Co is an advertising site for independent Dallas fence contractors. It does not do the work, and every price below is what one firm advertises on its own page, not a quote from this site. If you are weighing a repair against a new run, read fence installation in Dallas and what fences cost in Dallas too, then call (214) 555-0137 to describe the job.

features.title: Leaning sections
features.desc: A leaning run is often a post problem rather than a picket problem. One Dallas firm advertises $300 to $800 per section for straightening 10 to 30 ft.

features.title: Broken and rotted posts
features.desc: A contractor pulls the post and sets a new one in a concrete footing. One Dallas firm advertises $150 to $400 for a single post, and a Fort Worth firm $180 to $350.

features.title: Loose and missing pickets
features.desc: Board and picket swaps are the smaller repairs, but the numbers are counted differently: a Fort Worth firm advertises $8 to $15 per picket, a Dallas firm $25 to $60 per board installed. Ask what each quote counts.

features.title: Storm and wind damage
features.desc: The National Weather Service counts North Texas storms with 58 mph winds as severe. One DFW firm advertises storm damage repair at $300 to $1,200, quoted by the section.

features.title: Sagging wood gates
features.desc: A gate that drags or will not latch may need only hardware. One DFW firm advertises $60 to $150 for a latch or hinges, and a Dallas firm $400 to $1,200 for hardware and a drop.

features.title: Steel posts as an option
features.desc: Ask whether steel posts are an option for your run and how they change the quote. This site has no sourced price for them, so get the figure in writing.

sections.heading: What a fence repair scope covers
sections.html:
A repair quote should name each item rather than say 'fix fence'. Dallas-area firms that publish repair prices split the work into the same few categories:

  • Post replacement, with a new concrete footing
  • Board or picket replacement, including cedar pickets and any cap and trim that has to match
  • Straightening or resetting a leaning section
  • Panel rebuilds after wind or storm damage
  • Gate hardware, latch and hinge work, or a gate drop

The process worth asking for starts with the whole run, not the one spot you noticed. A contractor should check every post and rail, because a rotted post at one end often has neighbours in similar shape. It is better to hear that before the work starts than halfway through.

Much of the Dallas area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture, which can move posts over time. This site does not quote a post depth, because the sources conflict. Ask the contractor what footing they will use and have it written into the quote.

sections.heading: Repair or replace: how contractors decide
sections.html:
No published rule says a fence is past repair at a given age or percentage, and this site will not make one up. A contractor weighs the condition of the posts, how much of the run is affected, and what the repair costs against a new run. Rotten posts along the whole run, or a fence near the end of its life, are the usual reasons a contractor steers toward replacement, because fixing one section just moves the failure down the line.

Ask for both numbers on paper: a repair quote and a replacement quote for the same run. The gap between them is the figure to look at. For the replacement side, see fence installation and fence cost.

Steel posts are a repair option worth raising. The questions for the contractor are what they add to the quote and how they tie into your existing rails and pickets. No sourced Dallas price for steel posts exists on this site, so treat any figure as that contractor's own.

City rules can change the math. Plano's handout says a permit is not required for repairs to existing fences not exceeding 25% of the fence area in a 12-month period. Carrollton's page asks for a permit when repairing more than 20 ft, and Richardson's page requires one when replacing 25% or more. The City of Dallas guide says no permit is needed for fences 4 ft or less in a front yard or 6 ft or less elsewhere, except in historic, conservation and planned development districts, so confirm with the City and your HOA before work starts.

sections.heading: What Dallas-area firms advertise for fence repair
sections.html:
These are figures individual firms publish on their own pages, and they do not agree with each other. Use them to spot a quote far outside the range, not as a price from this site.

  • One Dallas firm: single post pulled and reset in a new concrete footing, $150 to $400; board replacement, $25 to $60 per board installed; straightening a leaning section (10 to 30 ft), $300 to $800 per section; full panel rebuild after wind (20 to 50 ft), $1,200 to $3,500; gate hardware and drop, $400 to $1,200.
  • One DFW firm: reset a leaning post, $75 to $200; replace 5 to 10 boards, $200 to $500; fix a gate latch or hinges, $60 to $150; storm damage repair, $300 to $1,200.
  • One Fort Worth firm: $180 to $350 per post replacement; $8 to $15 per picket; $450 to $1,500 for storm-damaged sections.
  • One DFW firm: fence repairs start at $450.
  • One more DFW firm: board and panel repairs typically $75 to $200 per section.

Nationally, the cost guide Fixr puts fence repair at $200 to $850 with an average of $500, and notes that many repair companies set minimum call-out charges. Another national guide cites minimum service charges of $150 to $300. This site has no sourced Dallas service-call minimum, so ask each contractor whether the quote includes one.

sections.heading: Before you hire: what the written quote should say
sections.html:
A written repair quote should list each item, the quantity and the price, so two quotes compare line by line. Ask for the post count and footing method, the board or picket count and material, any cap and trim, gate hardware, haul-away of old material, and what happens if more rotted posts turn up once the work starts. The contractor who quotes your job should be named on the paper.

Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level, but some cities register them, including Dallas, Richardson and Irving. Ask for the contractor's city registration and proof of insurance, and look at the documents themselves.

If posts are being reset, Texas811 says it is the contractor's responsibility to contact 811 two business days before digging when you hire one. If the fence is shared, TexasLawHelp says neighbours who both use a fence straddling the line both own it and share repair cost; that is general information, not legal advice. In many HOAs the association can still control fence type, so get written approval first.

For automatic gates, see gate repair in Dallas. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence. The same repair questions apply in Plano, Garland, Richardson, Mesquite, Irving and Carrollton, though each city sets its own permit thresholds.

faq.q: How much does fence repair cost in Dallas?
faq.a: It depends on what is broken, and firms publish different ranges. One Dallas firm advertises $150 to $400 for a single post with a new concrete footing and $300 to $800 for straightening a 10 to 30 ft leaning section, while a Fort Worth firm advertises $180 to $350 per post. The national cost guide Fixr puts repair at $200 to $850, with an average of $500. These are advertised figures, not quotes from this site.

faq.q: Should I repair a leaning fence or replace it?
faq.a: A leaning section can often be straightened or reset: one Dallas firm advertises $300 to $800 for a 10 to 30 ft section, and one DFW firm advertises $75 to $200 to reset a leaning post. If the posts are rotten along the whole run or the fence is near the end of its life, contractors tend to steer toward replacement. Ask for a repair quote and a replacement quote for the same run and compare them.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to repair a fence in Dallas?
faq.a: The City of Dallas guide says you do not need a permit for fences 4 ft or less in a front yard or 6 ft or less elsewhere, except in historic, conservation and planned development districts. Nearby cities differ: Plano exempts repairs that do not exceed 25% of the fence area in 12 months, and Carrollton asks for a permit when repairing more than 20 ft. Confirm with the City and your HOA before work starts.

faq.q: Who pays to repair a fence shared with a neighbor?
faq.a: TexasLawHelp says that if both neighbors use a fence straddling the boundary line, both own it and would share the cost of repairing and replacing it. A fence wholly on one lot belongs to that owner. This is general information, not legal advice, and no Texas statute on residential boundary-fence cost sharing was found. Show your neighbor the same written quote before work starts.

faq.q: What does storm damage fence repair cost in Dallas?
faq.a: One DFW firm advertises storm damage repair at $300 to $1,200, a Fort Worth firm advertises $450 to $1,500 for storm-damaged sections, and a Dallas firm advertises $1,200 to $3,500 for a full panel rebuild of 20 to 50 ft after wind. The National Weather Service counts North Texas thunderstorms with 58 mph winds as severe. Photograph the damage before anyone touches it, and ask each contractor to write the scope section by section.
